title: Rav Acha bar Minyomi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Avodah Zarah 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.7b.12) suggests that he came from Media. He tells Abaye: “A great man came from our place”—Nachum the Mede—“yet whatever he says, they tell him: ‘Let the matter sink into oblivion!’” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.7b.12.1) explains “from our place” as from Media.

He was Rav Nachman’s student: [Bava Kamma 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.106a.6) has him objecting to Rav Nachman, and [Bava Batra 148b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.148b.6) has him transmitting in Rav Nachman’s name. He discusses matters with Abaye in [Bava Batra 159b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.159b.8) and [Bava Batra 168b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.168b.9) and [Avodah Zarah 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.7b.12). Nedarim 47a has Rava objecting to him, and he is mentioned in [Yevamot 94a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.94a.3). Kiddushin 46a has “the son of Rav Minyomi”; possibly he was the son of Minyomi, Rav Nachman’s colleague.[^3]

notes.text: מאתרין means “from our place”; it is not a place called Atrin. The critics reject Nachum’s statements. The proposal that the unnamed son of Minyomi is this Acha remains tentative.
“From our place” refers to Media in the reported explanation; the critics dismiss Nachum’s rulings, not this speaker. The identification of his father with Rav Nachman’s colleague remains tentative.

Rashi expressly glosses “from our place” as Media. In Bava Batra 148b, Acha transmits in Rav Nachman’s name. An adjacent transmission there uses Yosef bar Minyomi, and the shared patronymic leaves the proposed family relationships open. The supplied Nedarim and Kiddushin references are retained pending exact occurrence matches. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=328&lang=en).
